page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the E2 family, configured with 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory. The processing power is delivered by an Intel Xeon CPU operating at 2.2 GHz, featuring 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled and a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes a 55 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES cryptography, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks position this instance primarily in the lower tiers for compute-heavy workloads. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, data compression and decompression speeds are weak, with static web serving throughput limited to 2.66 GB/sec. However, memory performance is more balanced; the Passmark memory score ranks in the average range, although large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths remain in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU performance. The tradeoff is clear: while memory capacity and baseline memory operations are adequate, raw computational throughput and storage speed are limited. This configuration is best suited for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads such as caching layers, small databases, and lightweight text generation tasks.
